CRITICAL.impact_description: Protocol completely broken, funds at immediate risk, core functionality impossible

HIGH.impact_description: Severe economic loss, consensus manipulation, major functionality impairment

MEDIUM.impact_description: Moderate economic impact, griefing opportunities, UX degradation

LOW.impact_description: Minor inefficiencies, gas waste, theoretical attack vectors

VERY_HIGH.probability_description: Attack trivial to execute, no special conditions required

HIGH.probability_description: Attack requires minimal setup, common conditions

MEDIUM.probability_description: Attack requires specific timing or coordination

LOW.probability_description: Attack requires rare conditions or significant resources

VERY_LOW.probability_description: Attack theoretically possible but practically infeasible

findings.title: ERC4626 Share Transfer Bypass of Stake Locks
findings.description: StakeVault inherits ERC4626 but fails to override _update(), allowing users to transfer shares while bypassing contributor and validator stake locks. This completely negates the economic security model.

evidence_locations.code: contract StakeVault is ERC4626Upgradeable, AccessControlUpgradeable, PausableUpgradeable, UUPSUpgradeable, IStakeVault

exploit_scenario: User stakes tokens and sets validator capacity (locks stake)
User transfers ERC4626 shares to new address via transfer()
New address redeems shares for underlying tokens
Original account still shows locked stake but has no assets
Slashing operations fail, all stake operations break
findings.recommended_fix: Override _update() in StakeVault to check locked balances before transfers

findings.title: Missing ENGINE_ROLE Grant to QualityEngine
findings.description: StakeVault functions require ENGINE_ROLE, but QualityEngine.initialize() never grants this role to itself. Vault operations will revert, breaking core staking functionality.
exploit_scenario: Attempt to claimToContribute → vault.lockContributor() reverts with AccessControl error
findings.recommended_fix: Add engine.grantRole(C.ENGINE_ROLE, address(engine)); in QualityEngine.initialize()

findings.title: Validator Settlement Blocked on Contribution Rejection
findings.description: computeConsensus sets report.computed=true only on contribution acceptance, but settleValidator requires computed=true. Rejected contributions leave validators with permanently locked stake.
exploit_scenario: Validators attempt to settle → revert because computed=false
findings.recommended_fix: Set report.computed = true in both acceptance and rejection paths

findings.title: Consensus Oracle Manipulation via Sybil Coordination
findings.description: Consensus algorithm uses sqrt(stake) * reputation weighting, enabling coordinated Sybil attacks where multiple low-stake accounts can manipulate consensus outcomes.
exploit_scenario: Attacker creates 10 accounts with minimum stake (100 tokens each)
Each account commits identical manipulated scores
sqrt(100) * 1000 = 1000 weight per account, total 10k weight
Coordinated attack overwhelms honest validators with 10:1 weight ratio
findings.recommended_fix: Implement quadratic staking: weight = stakeAmount² * effectiveRep / PRECISION

findings.title: Escrow Underflow in Validator Settlement
findings.description: settleValidator deducts validator rewards without checking escrow sufficiency. Multiple settlements can deplete escrow before individual claims.
findings.recommended_fix: Add escrow balance check before reward deduction

findings.title: Consensus Storage Collision on Resubmission
findings.description: validatorConsensus mapping keyed by (projectId, index, validator) not by nonce. Resubmitted contributions at same index collide with previous consensus results.
findings.recommended_fix: Change mapping key to (projectId, index, nonce, validator)

findings.title: Zero-Stake Validation Bypass
findings.description: Zero-stake validations allowed despite minimum stake enforcement. ConsensusLib gives weight=1 to zero-stake validators, enabling Sybil attacks.
findings.recommended_fix: Enforce minimum stake > 0 and reject zero-stake validations

findings.title: Arithmetic Overflow in Consensus Calculation
findings.description: ConsensusLib.calculate() performs score * weight * PRECISION multiplication without overflow checks. Large stake amounts can cause uint256 overflow.
findings.recommended_fix: Use SafeMath or check for overflow in multiplications

findings.title: Free Option via Ghost Validator Commitments
findings.description: Validators can commit to validations without revealing, creating free options. They can observe consensus outcomes and only reveal if it benefits them.

evidence_locations.code: function cancelExpiredCommitment(bytes32 projectId, uint256 index, address validator) public

findings.recommended_fix: Implement forced reveal mechanism with time-based randomization

findings.title: Consensus Flash Loan Manipulation
findings.description: Flash loans can be used to temporarily inflate validator capacity for consensus manipulation. Borrowed stake can swing consensus outcomes without permanent cost.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement stake commitment lock periods and stake age requirements

findings.title: Project Funding Sandwich Attack
findings.description: Project funding creates timing windows where attackers can front-run or back-run funding transactions to claim valuable indices through MEV.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement commit-reveal for index claiming with random assignment

findings.title: Validator Capacity Lock Without Unlock Path
findings.description: setValidatorCapacity locks stake but reduceValidatorCapacity only reduces committed capacity, not total capacity. No way to fully unlock validator stake.
findings.recommended_fix: Add unlockValidatorCapacity() function callable by validators

findings.title: No Timelock on UUPS Upgrades
findings.description: UUPS upgrade authorization requires only DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE with no timelock delay. Compromised admin key enables instant protocol takeover.
findings.recommended_fix: Deploy behind TimelockController with 48h minimum delay

findings.title: Reputation Manipulation via Zero Hash Bypass
findings.description: bytes32(0) commit hash bypasses duplicate prevention, allowing infinite zero-hash commits that manipulate reputation decay.
findings.recommended_fix: Reject zero hash commits explicitly

findings.title: Dispute Griefing via Bond Arbitrage
findings.description: Disputes can be opened with minimal bonds to grief contributors and delay reward release. Bond is returned if dispute is rejected.

evidence_locations.code:
uint256 bondAmount = (contrib.rewardRate * uint256($.disputeBondBps)) / C.BPS;
if (bondAmount == 0) bondAmount = 1;

findings.recommended_fix: Increase dispute bond scaling with project value

findings.title: Reputation Farming via Flash Projects
findings.description: Attackers can create flash-funded projects, contribute their own work, validate it positively, and extract reputation gains before abandoning.
findings.recommended_fix: Require minimum project duration before reputation extraction

findings.title: Validator Reward Dilution via Capacity Gaming
findings.description: Validators can game capacity allocation to maximize reward dilution. By committing maximum capacity but selectively revealing only for profitable validations.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement capacity commitment penalties for non-participation

findings.title: Originator Stake Timing Attack
findings.description: Originators can manipulate project funding timing to avoid stake requirements. By funding projects when originatorStakeRequirement is 0.
findings.recommended_fix: Make stake requirements fixed at project creation time

findings.title: Malicious Adapter Token Transfer Manipulation
findings.description: Adapter contracts can implement arbitrary logic in transferFrom calls. Malicious adapters could selectively fail or manipulate transfers.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate adapter contracts or remove adapter abstraction

findings.title: Fee-on-Transfer Token Accounting Errors
findings.description: fundProject handles fee-on-transfer tokens but other token operations may not account for actual received amounts.
findings.recommended_fix: Measure actual transferred amounts in all token operations

findings.title: ERC-7201 Storage Location Constants Unverified
findings.description: Hardcoded ERC-7201 storage location constants appear suspiciously 'clean' for cryptographic hashes. No on-chain verification exists.
findings.recommended_fix: Add on-chain verification of storage location derivation

findings.title: Fee Rounding Bias in Multi-Fee Waterfall
findings.description: Multiple sequential fee deductions create cumulative rounding bias. Each fee uses integer division, favoring the protocol treasury.

evidence_locations.code:
// Deduct protocol fee
uint256 protocolFee = (received * $.protocolFeeBps) / C.BPS;

findings.recommended_fix: Use higher precision arithmetic or reverse fee order

findings.title: Reward Claiming Gas Griefing
findings.description: Universal claimReward function allows griefing by repeatedly claiming zero amounts or using gas-intensive token transfers.
findings.recommended_fix: Add minimum claim thresholds and claim cooldowns

phases.name: Critical Path
phases.description: Fix core functionality and security foundations

testing_requirements: Unit tests for all fixes (100% coverage on critical paths)
Fuzz testing re-run with zero new critical issues
Economic analysis showing acceptable residual risk

success_criteria.residual_risk: Average risk score < 6 for remaining issues
